new.stem_en: Which HTML element is the most appropriate for the main navigation links of a page?
new.expl_en: The nav element is a semantic landmark for major navigation blocks; div and span carry no meaning.

en: nav, which marks the block as primary navigation
div, which groups the links without some meaning
section, which marks the block as a topical region
aside, which marks the block as tangential content

new.stem_en: In the CSS box model, which property sits between the content and the border?
new.expl_en: Padding is the space between content and border; margin is outside the border.

en: padding
margin
outline
gap

new.stem_en: You want three cards in one row that wrap onto the next line on narrow screens. Which CSS fits best?
new.expl_en: A flex container with flex-wrap lets items share a row and wrap when space runs out.

en: display: flex with flex-wrap: wrap on the parent for the project
display: block with float: none on each card
position: absolute with a fixed left value on each card
display: inline with a fixed width set in pixels on each card in most teams

new.stem_en: A rule .btn.primary { color: white } and a rule .primary { color: black } both match an element. Which colour applies?
new.expl_en: The selector .btn.primary has higher specificity (two classes) than .primary (one class), so white wins.

en: White, because the selector with two classes is more specific at that stage
Black, because the shorter selector is applied later in the cascade as the work grows
White, because rules written first usually override later ones
Black, because a single class usually beats a compound selector

new.stem_en: A fixed-width sidebar and a main column must fill the remaining width, side by side. Which CSS grid declaration does this?
new.expl_en: grid-template-columns: 240px 1fr gives a 240px column and lets the second column take the remaining space.

en: grid-template-columns: 240px 1fr
grid-template-columns: 240px 240px
grid-template-rows: 240px 1fr
grid-auto-flow: column 240px 1fr

new.stem_en: Which keyword declares a variable whose binding cannot be reassigned?
new.expl_en: const prevents reassignment of the binding; let and var allow it.

en: const
let
var
static

new.stem_en: What does [1, 2, 3].map(n => n * 2) return?
new.expl_en: map returns a new array with the callback applied to each element: [2, 4, 6].

en: A new array: [2, 4, 6]
The same array changed in place to [2, 4, 6]
The number 12 as the sum of doubles
An iterator that should be spread before use

new.stem_en: What does an async function always return?
new.expl_en: An async function wraps its return value in a Promise.

en: A Promise that resolves with the returned value from the start
The returned value itself without a wrapper
A callback that runs after the value is ready to use
An array holding the value together with a status flag

new.stem_en: What is logged by: console.log(0 == '0', 0 === '0')?
new.expl_en: == coerces types so 0 == '0' is true; === compares type and value so it is false.

en: true false
false true
true true
false false

new.stem_en: In what order are the logs printed? console.log('A'); setTimeout(() => console.log('B'), 0); Promise.resolve().then(() => console.log('C')); console.log('D');
new.expl_en: Synchronous code runs first (A, D), then the promise microtask (C), then the timer callback (B).

en: A D C B
A D B C
A C D B
A B C D

new.stem_en: What is the main benefit of TypeScript over plain JavaScript?
new.expl_en: TypeScript adds static types that are checked at compile time, catching many errors before the code runs.

en: Types are checked before the code runs
Code runs faster in the browser engine
Code no longer needs to be compiled or bundled
Variables can be changed without declaring them

new.stem_en: Which declaration gives a function parameter the type string?
new.expl_en: The syntax is name: type, so (name: string) types the parameter.

en: function greet(name: string) {}
function greet(string name) {}
function greet(name <string>) {}
function greet(name as string) {}

new.stem_en: type Status = 'idle' | 'loading' | 'done'. What does assigning 'error' to a Status variable cause?
new.expl_en: A union of string literals only accepts those exact values, so 'error' is a compile-time type error.

en: A compile-time type error
A runtime exception when the line runs
Nothing, since strings are usually accepted
The value is converted to the nearest valid literal

new.stem_en: Which type is the safest choice for a value whose shape is not known yet and must be checked before use?
new.expl_en: unknown forces you to narrow the type before use; any switches the checks off.

en: unknown
some
rarely
void

new.stem_en: A function must return the same type it receives, for any type. Which signature expresses this?
new.expl_en: A generic type parameter T links the parameter and return types: function id<T>(x: T): T.

en: function id<T>(x: T): T
function id(x: some): some
function id(x: unknown): unknown
function id(x: object): object

new.stem_en: Which hook stores a value that, when changed, makes a React component render again?
new.expl_en: useState holds state and triggers a re-render when its setter is called.

en: useState
useRef
useMemo
useId

new.stem_en: How does a parent component give data to a child component?
new.expl_en: Data flows down through props.

en: Through props passed on the child element
Through a global variable the child imports
Through the DOM id of the child element
Through a callback registered on the window object

new.stem_en: A list is rendered with items.map(). Why does each element need a stable key prop?
new.expl_en: Keys let React match elements between renders so it updates, moves or removes the right ones.

en: It lets React match items between renders and update the right ones
It sets the id attribute that CSS selectors use on the item
It sorts the items in alphabetical order before display
It prevents the list from re-rendering when the data changes as the work grows

new.stem_en: useEffect(() => { fetchData(id) }, [id]). When does the effect run?
new.expl_en: The dependency array [id] makes the effect run after the first render and again whenever id changes.

en: After the first render and whenever id changes
Only once, after the first render of the component
After each render, whatever the value of id
Only when the component is removed from the page

new.stem_en: setCount(count + 1) is called three times in one click handler and the count goes up by only one. Which change fixes it?
new.expl_en: Updates based on the previous value should use the functional form, setCount(c => c + 1), because count is a stale snapshot within the handler.

en: Use the functional form: setCount(c => c + 1)
Wrap each call in setTimeout with a delay of zero
Move the three calls into a useEffect without a dependency array
Declare count with var instead of using useState

new.stem_en: Which of these is a front-end framework written and maintained by Google?
new.expl_en: Angular is developed by Google; Vue and Svelte are community projects, and Laravel is a PHP back-end framework.

en: Angular
Vue
Svelte
Laravel

new.stem_en: In Vue, which directive binds an input element to a data property in both directions?
new.expl_en: v-model creates two-way binding between a form input and data.

en: v-model
v-bind
v-on
v-show

new.stem_en: In Angular, which construct is used to share logic and data between several components?
new.expl_en: An injectable service, provided through dependency injection, is the standard way to share logic and state.

en: An injectable service
A template reference variable
A structural directive
A CSS view encapsulation rule

new.stem_en: In Vue 3, which function creates a reactive value that you read and write through .value?
new.expl_en: ref() wraps a primitive in a reactive object accessed through .value.

en: ref()
computed()
watch()
provide()

new.stem_en: Which Angular feature unsubscribes from an Observable automatically when it is used in a template?
new.expl_en: The async pipe subscribes and unsubscribes for you, avoiding memory leaks.

en: The async pipe
The ngModel directive
The trackBy function
The ngIf directive

new.stem_en: Which meta tag lets a page scale correctly on a phone screen?
new.expl_en: The viewport meta tag sets the layout width to the device width.

en: <meta name="viewport" content="width=device-width, initial-scale=1">
<meta name="mobile" content="responsive">
<meta name="screen" content="auto-fit">
<meta http-equiv="refresh" content="scale">

new.stem_en: What should the alt attribute of an informative image contain?
new.expl_en: Alt text should describe the meaning of the image for people who cannot see it.

en: A short description of what the image shows or means
The file name of the image including its file extension
The keywords that the page wants to rank for in search results
The pixel size of the image in width and height in practice

new.stem_en: A mobile-first stylesheet adds layout for wider screens. Which feature does that?
new.expl_en: Mobile-first CSS starts with the small-screen styles and adds min-width media queries for larger screens.

en: @media (min-width: 768px) { ... }
@media (max-width: 768px) { ... }
@import url(desktop.css)
@supports (display: grid) { ... }

new.stem_en: Normal body text has a contrast ratio of 3:1 against its background. What does WCAG AA say about it?
new.expl_en: WCAG AA requires at least 4.5:1 for normal text, so 3:1 fails.

en: It fails, because normal text needs at least 4.5:1
It passes, because 3:1 is the minimum for all text
It passes, as long as the text is bold or uppercase
It fails, because AA requires a ratio of at least 7:1

new.stem_en: A custom dropdown built from divs must work for keyboard and screen-reader users. What is the best approach?
new.expl_en: Use native elements where possible; otherwise add roles, states and full keyboard handling.

en: Use a native select, or add ARIA roles and keyboard handling
Add a title attribute on each div and keep the mouse handlers as they are
Hide the dropdown from assistive tools and show a link instead
Set tabindex to a large number so it is focused first for the business

new.stem_en: Which tool built into Chrome audits a page for performance and gives a score?
new.expl_en: Lighthouse audits performance, accessibility, best practices and SEO.

en: Lighthouse
Sources panel
Application panel
Elements panel

new.stem_en: What does the Largest Contentful Paint (LCP) metric measure?
new.expl_en: LCP measures how long the largest visible content element takes to render.

en: How long the largest visible element takes to render
How long the whole page takes to download in full by the browser
How quickly the page responds to the very first click
How much the layout shifts while the page loads in most cases

new.stem_en: Which attribute defers loading of images that are below the fold until they are near the viewport?
new.expl_en: loading="lazy" lets the browser delay offscreen images.

en: loading="lazy"
decoding="sync"
fetchpriority="high"
crossorigin="anonymous"

new.stem_en: A JavaScript bundle of 2 MB slows the first load. Which technique helps most?
new.expl_en: Code splitting loads only the code needed for the current route and defers the rest.

en: Code splitting so each route loads only what it needs
Minifying just the CSS files and then keeping one big script
Adding more fonts so the text renders sooner
Inlining most of the images as base64 text inside the script

new.stem_en: Cumulative Layout Shift is high because images pop in and push text down. What is the best fix?
new.expl_en: Reserving space with width and height (or aspect-ratio) stops content from jumping when images load.

en: Set width and height or aspect-ratio so space is reserved
Compress the images until they weigh less than 10 KB
Load the images after the page has finished loading
Move the images to a different domain so that they load faster

new.stem_en: In WordPress, what is a plugin?
new.expl_en: A plugin adds features to a WordPress site without changing core files.

en: Code that adds a feature to the site without editing core files in a real project
A template that controls just the colours and fonts of the whole site
A database table that stores the posts and pages of the site
A hosting plan that keeps the site online all day

new.stem_en: Which WordPress plugin is most commonly used to turn a site into an online shop?
new.expl_en: WooCommerce is the standard e-commerce plugin for WordPress.

en: WooCommerce
Akismet
Yoast SEO
Jetpack Boost

new.stem_en: You need to change the look of a theme without losing the changes on theme updates. What should you create?
new.expl_en: A child theme inherits from the parent and keeps customisations safe when the parent updates.

en: A child theme that inherits from the parent theme in most cases
A copy of the theme folder under a new name
A custom CSS file edited inside the plugin folder
A backup of the database taken before each update

new.stem_en: Which WordPress feature lets you define content such as Products or Events with their own fields and archives?
new.expl_en: Custom post types (often with custom fields) model new content kinds.

en: Custom post types
Widgets
Shortcodes
Menus

new.stem_en: A WordPress site is slow. Which combination gives the biggest improvement for the least effort?
new.expl_en: Page caching, image optimisation and removing unused plugins address the most common causes.

en: Page caching, optimised images and fewer unused plugins
A second theme installed next to the active one for the business
More widgets in the footer to balance the load
Disabling the admin login page to save requests in a real project

new.stem_en: What is a unit test of a front-end function?
new.expl_en: A unit test checks one small piece of logic in isolation.

en: A test that checks one small piece of logic in isolation
A test that clicks through the whole app in a real browser
A test that measures how long a page takes to load from the start
A test that compares screenshots across browsers

new.stem_en: Which tool is a popular test runner and assertion library for JavaScript projects?
new.expl_en: Jest runs tests and provides expect assertions and mocks.

en: Jest
Webpack
ESLint
Babel

new.stem_en: With React Testing Library, how should you usually find a button in a test?
new.expl_en: Queries by role and accessible name mirror how users find elements and keep tests resilient.

en: By its role and accessible name, such as getByRole('button', { name: 'Save' })
By the internal state variable names of the component
By its position index in the list of DOM nodes
By the generated CSS class name from the build tool

new.stem_en: A component calls a REST API on load. How should a unit test deal with the request?
new.expl_en: Mock the network call so the test is fast, deterministic and independent of the server.

en: Mock the request so the test is fast and repeatable in a real project
Call the real production API so the data is realistic
Skip the component because network code cannot be tested
Add a long timeout so the real server has time to answer

new.stem_en: An end-to-end test fails once in ten runs without any code change. What is this called, and what is the usual cause?
new.expl_en: A flaky test; typically caused by timing, shared state or missing waits for asynchronous work.

en: A flaky test, usually caused by timing or shared state
A regression, usually caused by a failed deployment for the project
A false negative, usually caused by far too few assertions
A smoke test, usually caused by a slow test runner
